# spec03 — a self-declared GENERATED file gets chezmoi's `create_` attribute, and a census that says so

Reading `litellm` to decide whether it belongs under `home/` (spec02) turned up
a live defect that nobody had filed. It is small to fix and it generalises, so
it is its own unit.

## The defect, measured

`home/dot_config/litellm/config.yaml` shipped in `0b77a71` as a plain managed
file. Its own first line reads:

```
# GENERATED by scripts/gen-litellm-config.py — regenerate, don't hand-edit.
```

and `04-shell/10` R9 has `litellm-gen-config` **rewrite the deployed target**
at run time. A plain managed file is restored on every `chezmoi apply`, and
`rr` — `04-shell/02` R3 — is `chezmoi update --force`. Measured in a scratch
apply against a copy of the real `home/`:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| apply | `~/.config/litellm/config.yaml` deployed |
| regenerate the target | (what `llm gen` does) |
| `chezmoi status` | `MM .config/litellm/config.yaml` — permanent drift |
| apply again | **the regenerated routes are gone** |

So the user runs `llm gen` when a provider changes, and the next `rr` silently
throws the result away. This is the same class the shell-init epic already
settled — `05-platform/03` keeps its generated files out of the managed set —
with the direction reversed: here the *managed* file eats the *generated* one.

## The fix, also measured

chezmoi's `create_` attribute writes a target only when it is absent and never
overwrites it. Renaming the source to `create_config.yaml` — the attribute is
not part of the deployed name, which stays `~/.config/litellm/config.yaml` —
gives, in the same fixture:

| step | result |
|---|---|
| apply | deployed, and still in `chezmoi managed` |
| regenerate, then `chezmoi status` | **clean** |
| apply again | **the regeneration survives** |
| delete the target, apply | **re-created**, so a fresh machine still gets a baseline |

## Acceptance

- [ ] `home/dot_config/litellm/config.yaml` is renamed to
      `create_config.yaml`, with `git mv` so the history follows. Content
      unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/shell-litellm.sh`'s `YAML=` follows the rename, and carries a
      comment saying `create_` is an attribute rather than part of the target
      name, and why it is load-bearing.
- [ ] `tests/managed-config.sh` gains a check: every file under `home/` whose
      first line declares it generated must carry the `create_` prefix. The
      predicate is the **file's own header**, not a hand-kept list, so it
      cannot go stale behind a rename.
- [ ] That check is a factored predicate reporting the offending paths, and
      its FAIL line names them.
- [ ] Its comment records the measured before/after table above, not a
      reasoned claim.
- [ ] `--selftest` plants a bare `GENERATED` file in a `scratch_tree` copy and
      the predicate reports it; renaming **the same file** to `create_*` —
      attribute added, content identical — reports nothing. That pairing is
      what proves the check is about the attribute rather than the filename.
- [ ] `--selftest` asserts the planted file was never created in the real tree.
- [ ] `bash tests/shell-litellm.sh` and `bash tests/managed-config.sh` both
      exit 0.
- [ ] `bash tests/deploy-skeleton.sh` exits 0 — it walks `home/` and is the
      gate a source rename would break next.

## Verify and Proof

```sh
git status --porcelain home/dot_config/litellm
bash tests/shell-litellm.sh;   echo "EXIT=$?"
bash tests/managed-config.sh;  echo "EXIT=$?"
bash tests/deploy-skeleton.sh; echo "EXIT=$?"
bash tests/managed-config.sh 2>&1 | grep -E 'create_'
bash tests/managed-config.sh --selftest 2>&1 | grep -E 'GENERATED|create_'
```
